title: Asynchronous Distributed-Memory Parallel Algorithms for Influence Maximization
problem: Influence maximization requires finding k most influential nodes in large-scale graphs. State-of-the-art implementations rely on bulk-synchronous parallel algorithms with data replication, incurring high synchronization overhead and memory costs.
motivation: Efficiently identifying influential nodes in massive social networks and graphs is critical for viral marketing, network analysis, and understanding information diffusion patterns.
method: Instead of pausing all computation periodically to let every node catch up (bulk-synchronous parallelism), this approach lets compute nodes work asynchronously at their own pace and communicate only when needed. Each node holds its own slice of the graph data without redundant copies across nodes, cutting memory usage. On distributed-memory supercomputers like NERSC Perlmutter, this asynchronous communication improves network efficiency by sending data only when necessary rather than in synchronized batches.
key_novelty: Solving influence maximization with asynchronous algorithms where each compute node independently manages its slice of the graph, eliminating the need to replicate data or pause for synchronization.
contributions: Asynchronous distributed-memory parallel algorithms for influence maximization via martingales kernel operations
29.6x speedup over MPI-based state-of-the-art implementations on real-world and synthetic networks
First implementation to scale IMM to Twitter graph (41M nodes, 1.4B edges) in 200 seconds using 8K CPU cores
Improved memory scalability through elimination of data replication
